exposure: IOL indications (Grenoble Classification groups: Single cephalic pregnancy >=41 weeks of gestation, Single cephalic pregnancy with maternal pathology from 37 to 40+6 WG, Single cephalic pregnancy with foetal pathology from 37 to 40+6 WG)
cohort: The study included 54,089 women who delivered a live-born infant in a French region between 2020 and 2023.
finding: The overall prevalence of induction of labour (IOL) significantly increased from 2020 to 2023, primarily driven by higher rates in pregnancies ≥41 weeks of gestation and those with maternal or foetal pathology, which also saw increases in adverse maternal outcomes.
mod_finding: Increased emergency caesarean rates were observed in pregnancies ≥41 weeks of gestation (Group-5) and those with foetal pathology from 37 to 40+6 WG (Group-7) following IOL.
gest_age: Included pregnancies with gestational ages of >=41 weeks, and between 37 and 40+6 weeks depending on IOL indication groups.
